passage:
Subject: Re: how did you find your therapist?
Hi Urmila,
Of course I'll share. First, I ignored the short videos of life coaches promising to "fix anxiety in seven days". I looked for people who listed their qualifications and registration, and I asked my family doctor for two names.
The first therapist was qualified, but we just didn't click. I felt rushed, and I nearly gave up on therapy altogether. My sister said, "You wouldn't stop seeing doctors after one bad one." So I tried the second name. A much better fit.
Around the fourth session it got harder before it got easier. I wanted to quit. I'm glad I didn't.
One more thing, and I mean it: if you ever feel unsafe, don't wait for an appointment. Call a helpline or go to the emergency department that same day.
Proud of you for looking.
Sudha

qa.q: Why did Sudha nearly give up on therapy?
qa.a: The first therapist didn't feel like a fit and Sudha felt rushed and discouraged.

qa.q: Which choice kept Sudha from quitting too early?
qa.a: After Sudha's sister's reminder, Sudha tried the second qualified therapist and stayed on through the hard fourth session.

qa.q: How might Urmila feel reading "Proud of you for looking"?
qa.a: Urmila may feel encouraged that searching for help is a strength, not something to be embarrassed about.

grounding: It shows a young adult choosing registered professionals, changing therapist when the fit was wrong, not quitting early, and urging emergency help in a crisis.

passage: Elizabeth, people always ask me how I "found the right person", as if it were luck. It wasn't. I'm Binita. When I moved to London for work at twenty-four, I was low for months. A colleague recommended a "healer" with no training who charged a fortune. I said no, and checked the professional register online instead. I tried two therapists before one felt right: someone who let me take my time and still challenged me. But the part I really want your listeners to hear is about one night in March, when my thoughts got frightening and I didn't feel safe. My next session was four days away. The old me would have waited. Instead I rang the crisis helpline, and they stayed on the phone while my flatmate took me to A&E. My therapist said later that was exactly the right call.

qa.q: What was Binita feeling on that night in March?
qa.a: Binita felt frightened and unsafe because the thoughts had become scary.

qa.q: What choice did Binita make that night instead of waiting four days?
qa.a: Binita rang the crisis helpline and went to A&E with the flatmate, rather than waiting for the next session.

qa.q: How might Binita's therapist see that choice?
qa.a: The therapist saw it as exactly the right call, since a crisis needs help straight away, not at the next appointment.

grounding: It shows a young adult avoiding an untrained healer, checking registered therapists until the fit was right, and going to a helpline and emergency care in a crisis.
